# Startup readback: AI-17

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Implement durable inter-agent requests and explicit ownership transfers on the canonical runtime so Planner and specialists can request bounded work, return evidence to the initiating owner, and resume without hidden model recursion or lost context.

1. A request has a typed destination/objective/output contract, bounded context/evidence references, source run/message, owner, status, deterministic idempotency key, deadline and result reference; invalid routing/capability requests fail clearly.
2. Ownership transfer is a durable, audited event separate from an information request. Specialist results return to the original run/conversation with correlation and evidence, while direct user-to-specialist conversations remain valid.
3. Depth/duplicate-cycle limits, timeout/failure escalation and dependency waits are deterministic and recoverable: no unbounded nested calls, duplicate completed work, or orphaned silent requests.

## Implementation and boundaries

After the readback and integration review, trace the current AI-14 request/handoff contracts, AI-15 run and manager-core lifecycle, AI-16 capability/tool policy, and their direct callers/consumers. Reuse existing request/handoff entities, services, RPCs and fixture paths. Implement only missing request state transitions, deterministic routing and safe queue/orchestrator resumption; persist ownership history and surface timeouts/failures through the existing attention/trace path. Keep cost/correlation ownership with the existing AI-20/AI-19 paths. Any shared cost or acceptance interface change must be coordinated with the parent before editing.

Do not add a second conversation/request store, prompt-only delegation, synchronous recursive model-to-model loops, broad service-role table access, new AI policy/budget logic, or manager-specific business reasoning. Do not make Planner a mandatory hop for a direct specialist conversation. No subagents are planned; one owner remains accountable through release.

## Hosted proof and readiness

AI-17 explicitly requires one real staging Planner→specialist journey that persists the request, specialist run, reply and consolidated result. Include one real durable ownership handoff if the changed service path persists that transition. Keep deliberate circular delegation, duplicate request and failure/timeout matrices local. Use the exact immutable candidate, staging lease and current acceptance-evidence producer→validator→consumer contract; verify applicable DB grants/fixtures before dispatch. If a headed app login/MFA prompt appears, tell the operator when the browser is ready and pause for their action. Bound any provider use to the existing approved workflow budget/model policy and record no secret or raw personal payload.

## Delegation and blockers

- **Frozen runtime interface (confirmed with parent):** every newly persisted request includes `destinationWorkflowCode`. The atomic create RPC resolves only an active `workflow_definitions` row owned by the requested destination manager and stores its ID on the canonical request; unknown, inactive, or cross-manager workflow codes are rejected. Queue only through the existing `workflow_execute` path. The RPC also verifies source manager/user/status, route path/depth and inherited `coalesce(source.cost_root_run_id, source.id)`, then creates the request, child run and queue item atomically. Completion binds the reply to that destination run, records failure attention and resumes the source only after all sibling requests finish. Handoff remains a separate durable record backed by the existing AI-14 handoff tables and ownership/event triggers.

- The AI-14 request transition trigger omits `waiting_for_dependency -> completed/rejected`, which the child result path requires. AI-17's migration overrides the transition function to allow these terminal results. Added `supabase/tests/ai17_inter_agent_transitions.sql`; after a local migration reset, its focused pgTAP proof passed 3/3. The broader `agent_runtime_contracts.sql` run still reported six handoff/audit failures (tests 30–32, 34, 36–37), so it is recorded separately from the AI-17 regression result. The Linear context lookup again returned `Tool get_agent_context not found`.
